Source: table.md

Below is a reference table of the codes in predictorMatrix, collected from the documentation and the source of mice 3.19.17, miceadds 3.20.10, micemd 1.11.0 and mitml 0.4.5.

For all methods, 0 means that the variable is not used. For the standard (single-level) methods, 1 means that the variable is a predictor, and there are no other codes.

Two-level methods that follow the mice convention

Method Package -2 1 2 3 4
2l.lmer, 2l.bin mice cluster fixed fixed + random as 1¹ as 1¹
2l.norm mice cluster ignored² fixed + random – –
2l.pan mice cluster fixed fixed + random fixed + cluster mean fixed + random + cluster mean
2l.pmm, 2l.continuous, 2l.binary miceadds cluster fixed fixed + random fixed + cluster mean fixed + random + cluster mean
2l.2stage.norm, .pmm, .bin, .pois micemd cluster fixed³ fixed + random as 1³ as 1³
2l.glm.norm, .bin, .pois micemd cluster fixed³ fixed + random as 1³ as 1³
2l.jomo micemd cluster included⁴ included⁴ – –
2lonly.mean mice cluster – – – –
2lonly.norm, 2lonly.pmm mice cluster predictor predictor – –
2lonly.function miceadds cluster⁵ predictor – – –

Methods that give the codes another meaning

Method Package Codes
2l.contextual.pmm, 2l.contextual.norm miceadds -2 cluster, 1 predictor, 2 predictor + cluster mean (contextual effect)
2l.latentgroupmean.ml, 2l.latentgroupmean.mcmc miceadds -2 cluster, 1 predictor, 2 predictor + latent group mean
2l.groupmean, 2l.groupmean.elim miceadds -2 cluster, 1 or 2 variable whose cluster mean is computed
plausible.values miceadds -2 cluster, 1 predictor, 2 predictor + cluster mean, 3 item of the scale to be imputed
pls, 2l.pls2 miceadds -2 cluster (adds the cluster mean of y, leaving out the case itself), 1 predictor, 4 interactions with all other predictors, 5 quadratic term, 6 left out of the interactions
2l.2stage.heckman micemd -2 cluster, 2 predictor in the outcome and selection equations, -3 selection equation only, -4 outcome equation only (all predictors have random effects)
ml.lmer miceadds 1 fixed effect; set levels and random slopes with the arguments levels_id, variables_levels and random_slopes, not with codes

Multivariate methods for blocks (mitml codes)

For jomoImpute and panImpute, the row of the block in predictorMatrix is passed to mitml as its type argument. These codes differ from the mice convention: in mitml, 2 is a fixed effect and 3 a random effect.

Code Meaning in mitml::jomoImpute() and mitml::panImpute()
1 target variable with missing data
2 predictor with a fixed effect on all targets (complete)
3 predictor with a random effect on all targets (complete)
-1 grouping variable; the model is fitted separately within each group
-2 cluster indicator
0 not in the model

panImpute requires a cluster indicator (-2) and at least one random effect. Since #790, variables in the block are always passed as targets (1) unless another code is set.

Notes

  1. 2l.lmer and 2l.bin take all positive codes as fixed effects and 2 as a random effect. Codes 3 and 4 give no error, but they also add no cluster mean.
  2. 2l.norm uses only -2 and 2. Predictors with code 1 are dropped without a warning. The documentation advises using 2 for all predictors.
  3. micemd documents only -2 and 2, but the source takes all positive codes as fixed effects, as in 2l.lmer.
  4. micemd 2l.jomo includes all variables with a positive code in a joint random-intercept model. Code 2 does not add a random slope.
  5. miceadds recommends the argument cluster_var over code -2.
